28: One mode [of betrothal] cannot be derived from another [mode of betrothal], etc. - [the Gemara] asks as follows: the Tanna who earlier asked regarding each [method of betrothal] "can't it be derived using a logical derivation", and who then concluded that they cannot be derived logically, but require scriptural support -- why do we require scriptural support for each of them? Granted that one mode cannot be derived logically from another; but let one mode be derived from two others using the "just as we find in the common denominator of these" argument: that they are capable of acquiring in general and are capable of acquiring here [for betrothal]. "Then I shall even bring" the third [mode and derive its effectiveness from the other two]. All [three modes] are capable of acquiring in other circumstances: money and documents acquire a Hebrew maidservant, as will be stated later on [Kiddushin 14b] and sexual intercourse acquires a yevama.
Money and intercourse; their benefit is great - but a document of betrothal does not have any benefit, all that is written in it is "you are betrothed to me".
